claims.text: The FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
Removing Co lowers the stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Lower stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning at intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
Twinning enhances work-hardening capacity and the strength–ductility balance.
The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a solid solution with equiaxed grains.
The elements in the as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy are homogeneously distributed.
Differences in twinning activity should be most pronounced at approximately 200–400 K and strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
Deformation twins in the Co-free alloy are generated because of its lowered stacking-fault energy.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Twin-induced barriers increase strain hardening and improve ductility without compromising strength.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has a slightly higher stacking-fault energy than Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Under the specified conditions, CoCrFeMnNi is less likely to twin and relies primarily on dislocation glide.
Within the specified window, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have greater twinning activity than CoCrFeMnNi.
Within the specified window, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher strain-hardening rates than CoCrFeMnNi.
Within the specified window, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a superior strength–ductility balance relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
At very high strain rates or extreme temperatures, other deformation mechanisms may dominate and obscure the twinning effect.
